semantic_atoms.claim: Historical ToolExecutor.execute checked whether approval was required before dispatch and returned approval_required without executing when approval was missing. This was real source-level pre-execution gating on that path, unlike current stern.zulassen() generic bookkeeping which intentionally does not block normal Claude Code tool execution.
semantic_atoms.boundary: Source presence does not prove all historical runtime paths used this executor. skip_approval is a caller-controlled bypass and therefore is not acceptable as canonical Frankenstein-2.0 effect authority.

semantic_atoms.claim: Historical AgentLoop used a fixed _SAFE_AUTO_APPROVE tool-name set. Listed tools called executor.execute(..., skip_approval=True); other tools obtained an approval_id, waited for a response, and executed with skip_approval=True only after approval.
semantic_atoms.boundary: Tool-name allowlisting can drift from semantic effect risk and cannot replace typed capability/effect classification.

semantic_atoms.claim: Historical approval requests carried an approval_id plus tool_name, full tool_input, risk, reason and timestamp; responses were keyed by approval_id and queue files used file locks. The caller then executed its current tool call after the approval boolean returned.
semantic_atoms.boundary: The approval decision was not shown here to be cryptographically or structurally bound into the eventual executor invocation as an immutable request digest/token. Frankenstein-2.0 should bind approval/enforcement to exact invocation_id + request_digest + generation rather than rely on a boolean skip_approval handoff.

effect_contract: Keep the strongest historical idea: a mutating action can be stopped before dispatch.
Keep the strongest current-donor idea: request/outcome journaling with generation, idempotency, redaction and post-effect evidence.
Reject both weak handoffs: caller-controlled skip_approval booleans and a mutable session-wide current effect_id.
Bind one immutable invocation identity end-to-end: tool_use_id or generated invocation_id + request_digest + session_id + generation + causal_event_id.

Represent ADMISSION_DECISION, ENFORCEMENT_DECISION, EXECUTION_RECEIPT, WORLD_EFFECT_VERIFICATION, RESULT_REENTRY and COMPLETION_EVIDENCE as distinct typed states. Successful execution can never retroactively mint prior admission authority.
An approval/enforcement token is valid only for the exact invocation/request digest and generation; stale, mismatched or replayed decisions fail closed.
cancellation_contract: Preserve the current Realtime donor invariant that an interrupted/cancelled response discards still-pending function calls before local dispatch.

Generalize it to GRID: CANCELLED_BEFORE_SUBMISSION may prove non-dispatch only when no executor submission receipt exists; after possible submission, transport uncertainty becomes OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is verified rather than blindly replayed.
world_substrate_contract: Carry KNOWN, UNKNOWN, CONFLICT and NOT_COMPUTED as typed epistemic states outside vectors.

Adopt the current Perception Control pattern: protected COMPUTE_OFF or taint-blocked dependencies remain NOT_COMPUTED through derived operators; downstream vector similarity/decomposition may not reconstruct a disabled variable as a policy bypass.
